submission.natural_language_explanation:
The pole marks the last token of a typographic unit: it fires on the word immediately before the bare '
' that ends a hard-wrapped line in running text (code comments, licence headers, Gutenberg-style and other word-wrapped documents) and on the word immediately before a closing emphasis marker '_' or '*' (as in _hetairae_ or *could*), once several consistent line ends have established the wrap, so a 30-token passage usually will not fire. It stays near zero when the next token is ordinary text or ordinary punctuation (unwrapped prose, a sentence-final '.
', a paragraph '

', a comma, a period, a closing parenthesis), and its peaks sit where the model's own next-token mass is already mostly on that delimiter; zero-ablating the pole shifts the next-token distribution only slightly (KL about 2e-4), so the harness measures the mechanism as retrospective.

rival_explanations:
It is a general end-of-line marker rather than a mid-sentence-wrap marker, so it should also fire before a sentence-final '.
' and before a paragraph '

'.
It is a formatting-punctuation promoter triggered by any delimiter-character token, so it should fire as strongly before a comma, a period or a closing parenthesis as before a newline.

It detects the formatting register of the whole passage (code comment, licence header, markup) rather than the position of one delimiter, so it should fire anywhere inside such a passage, mid-line included.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
On the morning of the inspection the foreman walked through the sheds and noted that the roof of the third bay had been patched during the winter, that the drainage channel along the eastern wall was clear, and that the new lamps had been fitted above the loading dock,
though the electrician had not yet signed off the work. He wrote a short memorandum for the file and sent a copy to the office, where it was entered in the register and passed to the committee that meets on Thursdays, which had asked for an update before the end of the term. The committee had been formed after the fire at the mill, when the insurers insisted that every site in the valley be surveyed and that a written schedule of repairs be lodged with the county. The foreman had read the earlier reports with some care, and he knew that the inspectors were chiefly interested in the state of the boilers, the width of the stairways, and the number of exits from the upper floors, none of which had changed since the previous survey. The engineer said that the feed pump had been noisy for a fortnight and that a replacement bearing had been ordered from the works at the other end of the valley, though the delivery might be delayed if the river rose again. The foreman folded the memorandum into his coat and walked slowly to the gate, thinking about the questions the committee would ask and the answers he would have to give before the end of the month.

readings.explanation:
The pole marks the last token of a typographic unit: it fires on the word immediately before the bare '
' that ends a hard-wrapped line in running text (code comments, licence headers, Gutenberg-style and other word-wrapped documents) and on the word immediately before a closing emphasis marker '_' or '*' (as in _hetairae_ or *could*), once several consistent line ends have established the wrap, so a 30-token passage usually will not fire. It stays near zero when the next token is ordinary text or ordinary punctuation (unwrapped prose, a sentence-final '.
', a paragraph '

', a comma, a period, a closing parenthesis), and its peaks sit where the model's own next-token mass is already mostly on that delimiter; zero-ablating the pole shifts the next-token distribution only slightly (KL about 2e-4), so the harness measures the mechanism as retrospective.

It is a general end-of-line marker rather than a mid-sentence-wrap marker, so it should also fire before a sentence-final '.
' and before a paragraph '

'.
It is a formatting-punctuation promoter triggered by any delimiter-character token, so it should fire as strongly before a comma, a period or a closing parenthesis as before a newline.

It detects the formatting register of the whole passage (code comment, licence header, markup) rather than the position of one delimiter, so it should fire anywhere inside such a passage, mid-line included.
